partial_case.facts: The landlord is London Borough of Camden Council and the occupancy is a secure tenancy. The property is a 2-bedroom maisonette and the resident lives with her husband. The complaint concerned the landlord's handling of reports of no heating and hot water and complaint handling. On 27 November 2024 the resident complained to the landlord about a lack of heating and hot water, saying she had not had working heating since winter 2020 and raising issues including health and safety concerns, health impact, loss of earnings, and the financial impact of running electric heaters. On 8 January 2025 the landlord provided its stage 1 response, upheld the complaint due to intermittent loss of service, and told the resident about a heating rebate. On 14 January 2025 the resident escalated the complaint to stage 2, seeking heating repair and compensation for extra electricity costs, stress, time spent dealing with the issues, and loss of wages while waiting for contractors who did not turn up. On 21 March 2025 the landlord provided its stage 2 response, referred to repairs, a major leak on the estate, and a planned new heating and hot water system, and upheld the complaint with an apology and a heating rebate offer. The resident remained dissatisfied and wanted working heating in time for winter, a meeting with a housing officer, compensation for additional electricity expenses, and compensation for time taken off work.

orders: Payment of £175 compensation, made up of £75 for service failure in handling reports of no heating or hot water and £100 for maladministration in complaint handling
Written update about installation of a new heating and hot water system

The landlord communicated poorly with the resident and did not manage her expectations about when a new heating system would be installed.
The landlord did not comply with the response timescales set out in its complaints policy.

It failed to address all points raised by the resident in its responses and there was confusion within the landlord about the handling of this complaint. This led to a confusing and frustrating experience for the resident.
